range: Reading, morphology, language and thought, modalities
lead: These pages turn the Module III decks on reading, past-tense morphology, language and thought, and sign and Braille into topic summaries, a full final review guide, experiment cards, contrasts and common traps. The final review deck also repeats earlier material on aphasia, the critical period, semantic blocking and speech perception, and the review guide answers those pages too.
flags: There is no answer key for LING406, so every answer here is written from the Module III decks.
The phonological dyslexia study cited as Cacciopo van Vliet and colleagues (2003) is usually spelled Caccappolo-van Vliet, and the published paper is usually dated 2004.
The DRC simulation of the Woollams patients cited as Coltheart and colleagues (2009) is usually dated 2010 (Coltheart, Tree and Saunders, Psychological Review).
Boroditsky and colleagues (2010, Cognition) is the paper by Boroditsky, Fuhrman and McCormick, which is usually cited as 2011 (Cognition volume 118).

French is grouped with the relatively regular scripts. French is usually described as fairly regular for reading but irregular for spelling, so it sits between English and Finnish in orthographic depth.
